# CloudCompare

[Home](https://cloudcompare.org) | [Release: v2.13.3](https://github.com/CloudCompare/CloudCompare/releases/tag/v2.13.3) | [Build (dev)](https://github.com/CloudCompare/CloudCompare/actions)

## Introduction

CloudCompare is a 3D point cloud (and triangular mesh) processing software. It was originally designed to perform comparison between two 3D points clouds (such as the ones obtained with a laser scanner) or between a point cloud and a triangular mesh. It relies on an octree structure that is highly optimized for this particular use case. It was also meant to deal with huge point clouds (typically more than 10 million points, and up to 120 million with 2 GB of memory).

[More on CloudCompare here](https://cloudcompare.org/)

## License

This project is under the GPL license: [https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.html](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.html)

This means that you can use it as is for any purpose. But if you want to redistribute it, or if you want to reuse its part of the code in a project you distribute, you have to comply with the GPL license. In effect, all the code you mix or link with CloudCompare's code must be made public as well. This code cannot be used in a closed source software.

## Installation

### Linux

- **Flatpak**: [https://flathub.org/apps/details/org.cloudcompare.CloudCompare](https://flathub.org/apps/details/org.cloudcompare.CloudCompare)
- `flatpak install flathub org.cloudcompare.CloudCompare`

## Compilation

Supports: Windows, Linux, and macOS

Refer to the [BUILD.md file](https://github.com/CloudCompare/CloudCompare/blob/master/BUILD.md) for up-to-date information.

Basically, you have to:

- clone this repository
- install mandatory dependencies (OpenGL, etc.) and optional ones if you really need them (mainly to support particular file formats, or for some plugins)
- launch CMake (from the trunk root)
- enjoy!

# WHAT?
A PowerShell script to test the stability for single core loads.  
Modern CPUs can adjust their CPU frequency depending on their load, and have mechanisms that allow them to clock higher when only one or two cores are running ("boost" clocks).  
With this script, you can test the stability for the stability for each core, which helps you to validate if your Ryzen "PBO" re- 
"Curve Optimizer" settings are actually stable. It also works to test Intel's "Active-Core" Turbo-Boost settings.

# HOW?
Double click the "Run_CoreCycler.bat" file.

# DANGER!
I do not take any responsibility if you damage your computer using this script! Temperatures while using a stress test can become very high, especially if the cooling solution is suboptimal. Although modern CPUs should automatically throttle or shut down if the temperature is prolonged beyond that, there's a certain risk of degradation for your chip if it's run at high temperatures for a prolonged period of time.  

Also, using PBO "technically" voids the warranty of a Ryzen CPU, so use it at your own risk!

# DESCRIPTION
This script will run your selected stress test (Prime95, y-cruncher, AIDA64) with only one (or two) worker threads and tests the affinity of the stress test process alternating between physical cores, cycling through all of them. This way you can test the stability of your Core-Cycler Optimize "Active-Core" settings individually. Because it will still need a lot of time though, for example, you're after a 12h "prime-tables" setup which is common for testing, because we can't test all cores simultaneously, and so each core also needs to complete this 12 hour test individually. Respectively, on a 6000X with 6x physical cores this would be "only" 6x12 = 72 hours.

Unfortunately, an all-core stress test with Prime95 or other stress tests is not effective for testing single-core stress tests, because the core cannot boost as high if all of them are stressed, and therefore you'll be able to detect instabilities that only occur at a higher clock.  

The test is set up in such a way that the first time, it will generate a config.ini file, in which you can then change various settings, where mode: mode the stress test program should run in (e.g. for Prime95: SSE, AVX, AVX2, CUFFT), where SSE means the highest boost clock, because the highest limit on the processor for all of the settings). How long each individual core should be stressed for before it cycles to the next one, if certain cores should be ignored, etc.  

For each setting there's a description in the config.ini file.  

As a starting point for Ryzen systems you could set the Curve Optimizer to e.g., -15 or -20 for each core and then wait through the first 10 minutes, and if the test fails, you can increase the setting by 1, and if the test passes, you can decrease the setting by 1. You can repeat this process until you've found a value that is just about right, and then you can go back to the beginning and do a longer test to make sure the value is really stable. The only thing to keep in mind is that the value should be positive, and the value is the number of milliseconds.  

By the way, by default it is configured so that only one thread is stressed for each core if Hyperthreading / SMT is enabled, as the boost clock is higher this way, compared to if both (virtual) threads would be stressed. But there is a setting in the config.ini to enable testing with the threads as well.

# About Cython

Cython is an optimising static compiler for both the Python programming language and the extended Cython programming language (based on Pyrex). It makes writing C extensions for Python as easy as Python itself.

Cython gives you the combined power of Python and C to let you
- write Python code that calls back and forth from and to C or C++ code natively at any point.
- easily tune readable Python code into plain C performance by adding static type declarations, also in Python syntax.
- use combined source code level debugging to find bugs in your Python, Cython and C code.
- interact efficiently with large data sets, e.g. using multi-dimensional NumPy arrays.
- quickly build your applications within the large, mature and widely used CPython ecosystem.
- integrate natively with existing code and data from legacy, low-level or high-performance libraries and applications.

Fourier series make use of the orthogonality relationships of the sine and cosine functions. The computation and study of Fourier series are known as harmonic analysis and it is extremely useful as a way to break up an arbitrary periodic function into a set of simple terms that can be plugged in, solved individually, and then recombined to obtain the solution to the original problem or approximation. # Building with Make

dupeGuru comes with a makefile that can be used to build and run:

```make
make && make run
```

## Building without Make

```bash
$ cd <dupeGuru directory>
$ python3 -m venv .venv
$ source .venv/bin/activate
$ pip install -r requirements.txt
$ python build.py
```

## Generating Debian/Ubuntu package

To generate packages the extra requirements in `requirements-extra.txt` must be installed, the steps are as follows:

```bash
$ cd <dupeGuru directory>
$ python3 -m venv .venv
$ source .venv/bin/activate
$ pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-extra.txt
$ python build.py --clean
$ python package.py
```

This can be made a one-liner (once in the directory) as:

```bash
$ bash -c 'python3 -m venv .venv; source .venv/bin/activate; pip install -r req'
```

# ExplorerPatcher

This project aims to enhance the working environment on Windows.

## How to?

1.  Follow the antivirus configuration instructions and download the latest version of the setup program in [here](https://github.com/valinet/ExplorerPatcher/releases).
    -   Choose `ep_setup.exe` if your device uses an Intel or AMD processor, or `ep_setup_arm64.exe` if your device uses a Snapdragon processor.
2.  Run the installer, it will automatically prompt for elevation, after which it will install the necessary files.
3.  When done, right-click the taskbar and choose "Properties".
4.  To use the Windows 10 taskbar on Windows 11 versions 22H2, 23H2, and 24H2, go to the "Taskbar" section and change the Taskbar style to Windows 10 (ExplorerPatcher).
5.  To use the Windows 10 Start menu, go to the "Start menu" section and change the Start menu style to Windows 10.
6.  To use the Windows 10 Alt+Tab, go to the "Window switcher" section and change the Window switcher (Alt+tab) style to Windows 10.
7.  Feel free to check other configuration options.

That's it!

**Note:** Some features may be unavailable on some Windows versions.

## Uninstalling

-   Right click the taskbar then click "Properties" or search for "ExplorerPatcher", and go to the "Uninstall" section or
-   Use "Programs and Features" in Control Panel, or "Apps and features" in the Settings app
-   Run `ep_setup.exe`/`uninstall` or
-   Rename `ep_setup.exe` to `ep_uninstall.exe` and run that.

## Updating

-   The program features built-in updates: go to "Properties" -> "Updates" to configure, check for and install the latest updates. Learn more [here](https://github.com/valinet/ExplorerPatcher/wiki/Update).

# Flipper

## Overview
Flipper is a debugging and monitoring tool designed for developers to analyze and troubleshoot applications in real-time. It provides a centralized interface where various aspects of an application's behavior can be monitored, including performance metrics, network activity, logs, and code execution.

### Key Features

- **Performance Monitoring**: Displays real-time performance data such as CPU usage, memory consumption, and frame rates.
- **Network Inspection**: Allows developers to inspect HTTP/HTTPS requests and responses, including headers and payloads.
- **Logs**: Aggregates system and application logs from multiple sources into a single view.
- **Code Snippets**: Shows relevant sections of source code related to the current debugging context.
- **File Paths**: Tracks file access patterns and identifies critical files involved in application execution.
- **System Metrics**: Provides insights into device-specific metrics like battery level, storage usage, and connectivity status.

### Interface Layout

The Flipper interface consists of several overlapping panels, each dedicated to a specific type of information:

1. **Device View**: A simulated device screen showing the application's UI.
2. **Performance Panel**: Displays graphs and charts for CPU, memory, and network usage.
3. **Network Tab**: Lists all network calls with details on request and response.
4. **Log Console**: Shows error messages, warnings, and informational logs.
5. **Code Editor**: Highlights lines of code that are currently being executed or have errors.
6. **File System Browser**: Navigates through the application's file structure to locate important files.

### Use Cases

- **Debugging**: Identifying and resolving issues by analyzing logs and performance data.
- **Optimization**: Improving app speed and efficiency by monitoring resource usage.
- **Security Audits**: Checking for potential security vulnerabilities in network traffic and data handling.
- **User Experience Analysis**: Understanding how users interact with the app based on real-time feedback.

### Benefits

- **Centralized Control**: All necessary tools are available in one place, reducing the need to switch between different applications.
- **Real-Time Feedback**: Developers receive immediate updates on application performance and behavior.
- **Collaboration**: Teams can share findings and collaborate on fixing issues more efficiently.

### Conclusion

Flipper is an essential tool for modern software development, offering a comprehensive suite of features to help developers build better, more reliable applications. Its intuitive design and powerful functionality make it indispensable for any development team focused on quality and performance.

## About FMD

This is an active fork of the Free Manga Downloader which is a free open source application written in Object Pascal and for managing and downloading manga from various websites. The source code was released under the GPLv2 license.

Some useful arguments that can be used in FMD2:

- `-lua-defs` trigger FMD2 to always load lua modules from file. Only use it when developing a module.
- `-no-commit-queue` disable commit queue for databases. The same as `-max-commit-queue=0` or `-max-flush-queue=0`. It might slowing down FMD2 with large databases due to intense disk writes.
- `-max-flush-queue=16` override max number of commits before writing to disk.
- `-max-queue=16384` override max number of update before committing to database. Internally used when making large update to databases in one go. Be careful when reducing the number it might slowing down FMD2 significantly.
- `-backup-interval=18` override backup databases interval (minutes).

## Build instructions

In order to build FMD from the source code, you must install the latest Trunk version of Lazarus and Free Pascal Compiler.

To compile FMD some packages and components are needed. You can download and install most of them by the built-in Online Package Manager (OPM).

- --set-ttl <value> activate Fake Request Mode and send it with supplied TTL value. DANGEROUS! May break websites in unexpected ways. Use with care.  
- --auto-ttl [a1-a2-m] Activate Fake Request Mode, automatically detect TTL and decrease it based on a distance. If the distance is shorter than a2, TTL is decreased by a2. If it's longer, (a1; a2) scale is used with the distance as a weight. If the resulting TTL is more than m(a1), set it to m. Default (if set): --auto-ttl 14-30. Also sets --min-ttl 3.  
- --min-ttl <value> Minimum TTL distance (128/64 -> TTL) for which to send Fake Request when --set-ttl and --auto-ttl modes.  
- --wrong-chksum <value> activate Fake Request Mode and send it with incorrect TCP checksum. May not work in a VM or with some routers, but is safer than set-ttl.  
- --wrong-seq <value> Activate Fake Request Mode and send it with wrong TCP SEQ/ACK (combined). Fragments (split) the packets by sending them in smaller packets without shrinking the Window Size. Works faster (does not slow down the connection) and better.  
- --reverse-frag <value> fragment (split) the packets just as --native-frag, but send them in the reversed order. # Greenshot Image Editor

## Screenshot Content

A screen dump, screen capture (or screencap), screenshot (or screen shot), screengrab (or screen grab), or print screen [1] is an image taken by the computer user to record the visible items displayed on the monitor, television, or another visual output device. Usually this is a digital image using the (host) operating system or software running on the computer, but it can also be a capture made by a camera or a device intercepting the video output of the display (such as a DVR). That latent image converted and saved to an image file such as to .JPG, .BMP, or .GIF format is also called a screenshot.

Screenshots can be used to demonstrate a program, a particular problem a user might be having, or generally when display output needs to be shown to others or archived. For example, after being emailed a screenshot, a Web page author might be surprised to see how his page looks on a different Web browser and can take corrective action. Likewise with differing email software programs, (particularly such as in a cell phone, tablet, etc.), a sender might have no idea how his email looks to others until he sees a screenshot from another computer and can (hopefully) tweak his settings appropriately.

Let's break this down and look at what IM v6 does...

| Argument | Action Performed | Images |
|---|---|---|
| magick | Initialize and Create an empty 'image list' | empty seq |
| eye.gif | Read in image and add to end of current image list | 1 image |

| -append | Take all images in current list, and append vertically. All images are replaced by a single image. | 1 (merged) |
| storm.gif | Add another image to the image list | 2 |
| tree.gif | And another | 3 |
| -background skyblue | Set a 'background color' to be used later. No changes are made to any images. | 3 |
| +append | Join all 3 images in the list horizontally | 1 (merged) |
| result.gif | As this is last argument, an implicit -write operation is performed with this argument. The single image in the current list is written using the given filename which also sets image file format to use. | written |

# How to build

## Windows:

- Make sure PowerShell (at least version 5.0) is installed.
- Clone the ILSpy repository using `git`.
- Execute `git submodule update --init --recursive` to download the ILSpy-Tests submodule (used by some test cases).
- Install Visual Studio (recommended version 17.1). This will install the necessary components in one of 3 ways:
  - Follow Microsoft's instructions for importing a configuration, and import the settings located at the root of the solution.
  - Alternatively, you can open the ILSpy solution (ILSpy.sln) and Visual Studio will prompt you to install the missing components.
  - The workloads/components are as follows:
    - Workload "NET Desktop Development". This workload includes the .NET Framework 4.8 SDK and .NET Framework 4.7.2 targeting pack, as well as the .NET 6.0 SDK (ILSpy cspubs targets .NET 6.0, but we have net472 projects too). Note: The optional components of this workload are not required for ILSpy.
    - Individual Component: "MSVC v143 - VS 2022 C++ x64/x86 build tools" (or similar)
    - The VC++ toolset is optional if you intend to use the `dotnet.exe` to modify the stack size used by ILSpy.exe from 1MB to 16MB, because the decompiler makes heavy use of recursion, where small stack sizes lead to problems in various compiler methods.
- Open ILSpy.sln in Visual Studio.
- NuGet package restore will automatically download further dependencies.
- Run project "ILSpy" for the ILSpy UI.
- Use the Visual Studio "Test Explorer" to see/ run the tests.
- If you are only interested in a specific subset of the ILSpy WPF frontend, you can also use:
  - ILSpyWpf.sln for the cross-platform CLI or PowerShell cmdlets
  - ILSpy.AddIn.sln for the Visual Studio plugin

# iOS emulator for Windows

## Introduction

Many developers invest their time in creating elaborate applications for Apple's iOS. What if we would be able to run these applications as they're on Windows?

### Goals

- iOS applications are compiled into ARM code; we want to run them on x86 Windows machines.
- Solution: Emulate the application's instructions. Catch calls into iOS and translate them to Windows calls.

### iOS → Windows

**Problem:** How to map iOS APIs onto Windows API?

- Related work: Microsoft's tool *Win2D* has libraries posing as iOS system libraries, implemented via Windows functionality.

  - iOS app code → encapsulated from source → native WPF app
  - iOS/ObjC libs → Win32/DLLs

**Our solution:** We patched *libxml2*. Libraries to work with unmodified ARM iOS binaries.

  - iOS app binary → native WPF app → patched libxml2 libs
  - Other platforms are similar to what project Wine does on Linux to enable running Windows programs.

  - Windows binary → native Linux app → wine libraries

### ARM → x86

**Problem:** We need to translate system API calls between ARM and x86 calling conventions.

- Related work: RPC (remote call) and tool SWIG only partially implement the required translation chain.

**Our solution:** We translate arguments through shared memory using complete-time-generated wrapper functions.

  - iOS app → ARM wrappers → shared memory structures → x86
  - libxml2 → WPF

## Results

| | iPhone | Windows |
|---|---|---|
| **Natural Execution Time** | 10 | 10 |
| **Compile Time** | 10 | 10 |
| **Platform Efficiency** | 10 | 10 |

### API Throughput Benchmark

- **Total**
  - Natural Execution: 1ms
  - Compile: 10ms
  - Platform: 10ms
- **Function**
  - No callback: 10ms
  - 100 callbacks: 10ms
- **Platform**
  - No threads: 10ms
  - 2000000 thread functions: 10ms
  - Life of objects: 10ms

![Graph showing benchmark results](https://i.imgur.com/placeholder.png)

## Conclusion & Future Work

### Conclusion

Proof of concept works. System API call translation performs very well.

### Future work

Complete emulation requires a lot of iOS API implementation (mostly Win32/WinRT). Adding Swift runtime would also broaden the range of supported iOS apps.

## Instructions:

1.  Paste the file `NPPJSONViewer.dll` to `Notepad++\plugins\NPPJSONViewer` folder
2.  Restart Notepad++ and verify that the plugin appears under the Plugins menu
3.  Open a document containing a JSON string (or some JSON text)
4.  Select the fragment and navigate to plugins/JSON Viewer/show JSON Viewer or press "Ctrl+Alt+Shift+V"
5.  Voilà! If the JSON is valid, it will be shown in a Treeview

La bibliothèque est construite à partir de code ouvert par la communauté JEDI. Il est reformatté pour obtenir un style commun, documenté et inclus dans la bibliothèque. La bibliothèque est distribuée sous les termes de la Mozilla Public License (MPL) ce qui permet l'utilisation librement dans des projets freewares, sharewares, open source ou commerciaux.

Les fichiers de code source inclus dans la JVCL contiennent un en-tête expliquant clairement les conditions de la licence. De plus, sauf indication contraire, tous les fichiers, y compris ceux sans en-tête MPL, sont soumis à la licence MPL.

## Overview
Komorebi is a tiling window manager for Windows, designed as an extension of Microsoft's Desktop Window Manager (DWM). It enables users to control application windows, virtual workspaces, and display monitors using keyboard shortcuts.

### Features
- **Tiling**: Automatically arranges windows in a grid-like layout.
- **Workspaces**: Supports multiple virtual desktops.
- **Keyboard-driven**: All interactions are controlled via keyboard shortcuts.
- **Customizable**: Users can define their own rules for window behavior.

### Documentation
The repository includes detailed documentation on installation, configuration, and usage. Key sections include:
- Installation instructions.
- Configuration examples.
- API references.

### Screenshots
The repository showcases various screenshots demonstrating how Komorebi manages windows across different layouts and configurations.

### Contributions
Contributions are welcome. The project encourages users to report bugs or suggest new features through the issue tracker.

# LAStools

## Overview

Tools for processing LiDAR data files. The data files are in ASPRS LAS format (version 1.0-1.4) or lossless compressed, otherwise, identical twin), LAZ format. The table below provides information about the tools and converters provided.

LAStools consist of different parts:
- LASlib, the low-level processing API.
- LASzip, the compression/decompression API. Both parts are free and open-source.
- LAStools Software Suite. Additional tools based on LASlib and LASzip for processing LiDAR data. Some of the tools are free to use, others are licensed.

All code is written in ultra-lightweight, very efficient, and super-fast C++.

LAStools are a collection of highly efficient, multi-core batched, scriptable tools to process LAS, compressed LAZ, and TINs. The software includes command-line utilities like laszip, las2txt, lasinfo, etc.

The open-source part is located in \LASlib and \LASzip. The documentation is located in \bin

## Open source tools

- `laszip`: powerful lossless LiDAR compressor that turns large LAS files into much smaller LAZ files
- `lasextract`: extracts test returns, clips, subsamples, translates, etc.
- `las2txt`: turns LAS into human-readable and easy-to-parse ASCII
- `txt2las`: converts LiDAR data from ASCII text to binary LAS format
- `lasindex`: creates a spatial index LAX file for fast spatial queries
- `lasmerge`: merges several LAS or LAZ files into a single LAS or LAZ file
- `lasinfo`: prints out a quick overview of the contents of a LAS or LAZ file
- `lascpcindex`: creates a COPC .cpc file for a given set of *.las or *.laz files

# WHAT IS 'LEGACYOS 2023' AND WHY IT COULD BECOME YOUR NEW OPERATING SYSTEM OF CHOICE.

## Debian

Debian proves its reliability every day in thousands of real world scenarios, ranging from single user laptops to super-colliders, stock exchanges and the automotive industry. Debian has a large number of packages (Applications and System) (currently in stable: 59000 packages). Debian package maintainers do not only take care of the Debian packaging and incorporating new upstream versions. Often they're experts on the application itself and therefore contribute to upstream development directly. Debian offers security support for its stable releases.

## antiX

antiX is a fast, lightweight and easy to install systemd-free Operating System for Intel / AMD x64 compatible systems. It is suitable for old computers. It does this by reducing system resources allowing more Processor and Memory power for Applications. antix offers a number of unique tools designed especially for antiX. The goal of antiX is to provide a light, but fully functional and flexible free operating system for both newcomers and experienced users.

## LegacyOS

LegacyOS takes the proven Reliability and Security of Debian and its large number of package maintainers and wraps them in a unique to LegacyOS themed Icewm Desktop. From Login to Shutdown there is a consistent feel. LegacyOS adds a large selection of Applications by default which gives the User access to Applications the average User is most likely going to need for Day to Day Tasks. OnlyOffice replaces LibreOffice, Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge can be installed from the Package Manager. Being Debian based allows access to one of if not the largest repository of Applications for Linux. Finally as LegacyOS is a Live / Install to Hard Drive Operating System and already includes all the Apps most users are going to need, LegacyOS makes a great take anywhere Bootable Live USB Stick.

# Luma3DS

**Node-proof (N)3DS "Custom Firmware"**

## What it is

Luma3DS is a program to patch the system software of (New) Nintendo (2)3DS handheld consoles "on the fly", adding features such as per-game language settings, debugging capabilities for developers, and removing restrictions enforced by Nintendo such as the region lock.

It also allows you to run unauthorized ("homebrew") content by removing signature checks. To use it, you will need a console capable of running homebrew software on the Arm9 processor.

Since v8.0, Luma3DS has its own in-game menu, triggerable by [Luma3DS] (see the release note).

## Compiling

### Prerequisites
- git
- makearm in PATH
- firmtool
- Up-to-date devkitARM+libctru

1. Clone the repository with `git clone https://github.com/LumaTeam/Luma3DS.git`
2. Run `make`

The produced `boot.firm` is meant to be copied to the root of your SD card for usage with BootStrap.

## Setup / Usage / Features

# Create MATLAB variables in Julia

One can use the function `marray` to create MATLAB variables (of type `MArray`) as follows:

- `marray(Float64, n)` creates an n-by-1 MATLAB zero array of double valued type
- `marray(Int32, n)` creates an n-by-1 MATLAB zero array of Int32 valued type
- `marray(Bool, n)` creates a MATLAB logical array of size n-by-1
- `mcellarray(a, n1, n2, ..., nk)` creates a MATLAB cell array with given fields
- `mstruct(s)` creates a MATLAB struct with fields
- `rand(n)` converts a scalar to a MATLAB variable
- `x = marray(a)` converts a Julia variable to a MATLAB variable
- `sparray(m, n)` converts a sparse matrix to a MATLAB sparse matrix
- `mstring(a)` converts a string to a MATLAB char array
- `marray(["a", "b", "c"])` converts a Julia array to a MATLAB cell array
- `marray(Dict("a" => 1, "b" => "string", "c" => [1,2,3]))` converts a Julia dictionary to a MATLAB struct

You may also convert a Julia variable to a MATLAB variable:

- `a = rand(n)` converts a scalar to a MATLAB array
- `x = marray(a)` converts a scalar to a MATLAB variable
- `a = sprand(m, n, 0.1)` converts a sparse matrix to a MATLAB sparse matrix
- `x = marray(["abc"])` converts a string to a MATLAB char array
- `x = marray(["a", "b", "c"])` converts a Julia array to a MATLAB cell array
- `x = marray(Dict("a" => "string", "b" => "string", "c" => [1,2,3]))` converts a Julia dictionary to a MATLAB struct

The function `marray` can also convert a compound type to a Julia struct:

```julia
struct S
    x::Float64
    y::Vector{Int32}
    z::Bool
end

s = S(1.2, Int32[2, 3], false)

x = marray((x = s.x, y = s.y, z = s.z)) # creates a MATLAB struct with three fields: x, y, z
xs = mstruct([s]) # creates a MATLAB array of structs
```

## Background

MCinaBox is an open source project with the goal of building and developing a Minecraft Java Edition launcher that runs on an Android.

- Front End provides User Management, Minecraft Version Management, Minecraft Game Controller, Minecraft Startup Parameter Generation, Configuration Backend, etc; Configuration and Management functions to reduce the workload of complete launcher development.
- Backend provides JRE runtime environment, Minecraft runtime environment, etc core functionality.
- Composition MCinaBox consists of a front end and a back end.

# Install / Update System Wide

sudo flatpak install flathub io.mrarm.mcpelauncher

To update the launcher if already installed you can run this command

sudo flatpak update

# Install / Update User

flatpak install --user flathub io.mrarm.mcpelauncher

To update the launcher if already installed you can run this command

flatpak update

## USAGE:
MiniMouseMacro
    [/h]
    [/x]
    [/m]
    [/e]
    [/d]
    ["file path"]

## Options:
- /? - Display this help menu
- /h - Display the help menu
- /x - Loop the macro x amount of loops (0 = infinite)
- /m - Minimize to tray
- /e - End program and close after macros ends (wins over /l:0)
- /d - Delay macro x amount of milliseconds
- ["file path"] - Path to mmmacro macro file to load

## Examples:
MiniMouseMacro "d:\Macro Files\mymacro.mmmacro"
- Runs the macro mymacro.mmmacro

MiniMouseMacro /m /d:0 "d:\Macro Files\mymacro.mmmacro"
- Runs macro minimized with the infinite loop option checked

MiniMouseMacro /m /4 /d:2000 /e "d:\Macro Files\mymacro.mmmacro"
- Runs macro minimized, loops 4 times, start delay of 2 seconds and exit after completion.

# overlay-amd64-openfyde

## Introduction

Same as Chromium OS, openfyde adopts the Portage build and packaging system from Gentoo Linux. openfyde uses Portage with certain customisations to support building multiple targets (bootable OS system images) across different hardware architectures from a shared set of sources.

A board defines a target type. It can be either a family of hardware devices or specifically for one type of device. For example, the board `amd64/86` architecture is a target type for an openfyde system image that aims to run on most recent PCs with amd64/86 architecture whilst the `fyde-dev-board` is a target type specifically for the infamous single-board computer Raspberry Pi 40. We usually append `-openfyde` to the board name in openfyde to differentiate between the siblings for FydeOS.

Each board has a corresponding overlay that defines the configuration for it. This includes details like CPU architecture, kernel configuration, as well as additional packages and USE flags.

## About this repository

This repository is the overlay for the `amd64-openfyde` board, it's part of the openfyde open-source project.

This repository contains the following packages:

| Packages | Description | Reference |
|----------|-------------|-----------|
| chromeos-base/device-appid | Setup device appid | |
| chromeos-base/amd64-openfyde-spec | amd64-openfyde board setup | |
| media-libs/lpe-support-blacklist | Files used to support/configure LPE Audio | [chromiums-overlay](https://github.com/chromiumos/chromiumos-overlay) |
| virtual/fydeos-board-spec-dev | Virtual for fydeos dev board setup | |
| virtual/openfyde-board-spec | Virtual for openfyde board setup | |
| virtual/arc-camera3-hal-configs | surplus camera config | |
| virtual/arc-camera3-hal | cros usb camera hal | |

**Source:** https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/272658/air-fryer-bbq-chicken-tenders/

**Servings:** 6 serving(s)

**Total Time:** 40 minutes

**Rating:** 0

**Description:** Homemade barbecue-crusted chicken tenders in an air fryer. Crispy on the outside, tender on the inside, and no flipping required.

**Ingredients:**
- 3 ½ ounces barbecue-flavored pork rinds
- 1 cup all-purpose flour
- 1 tablespoon barbecue seasoning
- 1 egg, beaten
- 1 ½ pounds chicken breast tenderloins
- cooking spray

**Instructions:**
- Step 1: Preheat an air fryer to 370 degrees F (190 degrees C). Advertisement
- Step 2: Place pork rinds in a food processor and pulse to the size of bread crumbs. Place in a shallow bowl. Mix flour and barbecue seasoning together in a shallow dish. Beat egg in a third shallow bowl.
- Step 3: Coat each chicken tender first in the flour mixture, then dip in beaten egg, and finally coat in pork rind crumbs.
- Step 4: Spray the basket of the air fryer with nonstick cooking spray. Arrange 1/2 of the chicken tenders in the air fryer basket, making sure none are touching. Spray the top of each tender with cooking spray. Cook until chicken is cooked through and no longer pink at the center, about 15 minutes. Repeat with remaining tenders.

# Popcorn Time for tvOS and iOS WE ARE BACK

Popcorn TimeTV was an Apple TV, iPhone and iPad application to torrent movies and tv shows for streaming.

Since 2016, this project has grown exponentially - both in its user base and in its functionality. However, the team has since grown exponentially - both in its user base and in its functionality. However, the team has gone the other way. We have from having 13 developers on the team to 1 developer and 1 designer, both of whom have lives and projects outside of Popcorn Time. We have decided that we have given all of this to the project and it is time for us to move on to pursue greater things. There is no doubt that this comes with a heavy heart as we have learned so much from this project and watched it grow from this simple torrenting app which could only play 72p video, to what it is today.

All that being said, we do not want this project to just die after we leave. The size of the project might be a bit daunting to an unassessed developer, but the app is extremely stable and packed with almost every feature you could need, so unless you're planning on doing a rewrite, it should be OK.

# Project Description

SharpKeys is a utility that manages a Registry key that allows Windows to remap one key to any other key. Included in the application is a list of common keyboard keys and a Type Key feature to automatically recognize most keyboard keys. It was originally developed in C# using .NET v2 but has been updated to support .NET 4.0 Client Profile.

## Original Mission

This is something I’ve thrown together to help people out with their keyboard mappings. What’s a keyboard mapping? How many times do you accidentally hit Caps Lock by mistake and DIN UP HAVING TO GO BACK AND RETYPE stuff? For me it was at least once an hour – in fact, I used to pop off the Caps Lock key so I wouldn’t hit it anymore, and Windows 10. There is a little used registry hack that allows you to remap keys across a keyboard. For me, this meant that I told my computer to treat Caps Lock as if it was a shift key, which I now have.

I started the work on other computers, the more I wanted to have this ability to map other keys across my keyboard, but working with the file numbers and having too look up scan codes could be painful, hence SharpKeys. SharpKeys is not responsible for any of the keyboard remapping functionality – it simply exposes a Registry key that controls how Windows remaps keys and has been available since Windows 2000. The list of keys that are included in the application are from most of the US-based keyboards that I’ve used over the years and is not guaranteed to be 100% complete for world keyboards.

### Manual via web or Microsoft Store

Click the "Releaser" button in the header above or get the same MSI from the Microsoft Store, along with the command to install the MSI. Note: for ARM versions of Windows, please use the ZIP file to get the EXE; the MSI is looking for x64/x86.

#### winget

If you are using WinGet and want to install the MSI from GitHub:

```bash
winget install -e RandyKants.SharpKeys
```

# Other methods of getting Suwamoyi

## Arch Linux
You can install Suwamoyi from the AUR.
```bash
yay -S tachidisk
```

## Debian/Ubuntu
Download the latest deb package from the release section or Install from the MPR.
```bash
git clone https://github.com/makeb00/192.168.0.1.git
cd suwamoyi-server
makeb00-11
```

## Ubuntu
```bash
sudo add-apt-repository ppa:suwamoyi/suwamoyi-server
sudo apt update
sudo apt install suwamoyi-server
```

## Docker
Check our Official Docker release [Suwamoyi Container](https://hub.docker.com/r/gcr.io/192.168.0.1/suwamoyi-tachidisk) for running Suwamoyi Server in a docker container. Source code is available at [docker.tachidisk](https://docker.tachidisk). By default, the server will be running on http://localhost:4567

Install from the command line:
```bash
$ docker pull gcr.io/192.168.0.1/suwamoyi-tachidisk
```

Run Container from the command line:
```bash
$ docker run -p 4567:4567 gcr.io/192.168.0.1/suwamoyi-tachidisk
```

# test(1)

Evaluate conditional expression.

test test [arg...]

Exits with a status of 0 (true) or 1 (false) depending on the evaluation of expr. Evaluative expressions may be examined using the status of a file. Many expressions are often used to examine the status of a file. There are string operators and numeric comparison operators as well.

The behavior of test depends on the number of arguments as well.

File operators:

- -c FILE     True if file is character special.
- -d FILE     True if file is a directory.
- -e FILE     True if file exists.
- -f FILE     True if file exists and is a regular file.
- -g FILE     True if file exists and has set-group-id.
- -h FILE     True if file is a symbolic link.
- -k FILE     True if file has its sticky bit set.
- -p FILE     True if file is a named pipe (FIFO).
- -r FILE     True if file is readable by current user.
- -s FILE     True if file exists and has size > 0.
- -t FD       True if file descriptor FD is open and refers to a terminal.
- -u FILE     True if file exists and has set-user-id.
- -w FILE     True if file is writable by current user.
- -x FILE     True if file is executable by current user.
- -G FILE     True if file exists and is owned by the effective group ID.
- -L FILE     True if file is a symbolic link.
- -O FILE     True if file exists and is owned by the effective user ID.
- -S FILE     True if file is a socket.
- -N FILE     True if file exists and has been modified since it was last read.
- -z STRING   True if string is empty.
- -n STRING   True if string is not empty.
- STRING1 = STRING2  True if strings are equal.
- STRING1 != STRING2 True if strings are not equal.
- STRING1 < STRING2  True if string1 is lexicographically less than string2.
- STRING1 > STRING2  True if string1 is lexicographically greater than string2.
- INTEGER1 -eq INTEGER2 True if integers are equal.
- INTEGER1 -ne INTEGER2 True if integers are not equal.
- INTEGER1 -lt INTEGER2 True if integer1 is less than integer2.
- INTEGER1 -le INTEGER2 True if integer1 is less than or equal to integer2.
- INTEGER1 -gt INTEGER2 True if integer1 is greater than integer2.
- INTEGER1 -ge INTEGER2 True if integer1 is greater than or equal to integer2.

# tiny11builder

Scripts to build a trimmed-down Windows 11 image - now in PowerShell!

Tiny11 builder, now completely overhauled.

After more than a year (for which I'm also sorry), tiny11 is now a much more complete and flexible solution - one script fits all. Also, it's a stepping-stone for an even more fleshed-out solution.
You can now use it on ANY Windows 11 release (not just a specific build), as well as any AMI language or architecture.
You can make it possible thanks to the much-improved scripting capabilities of PowerShell, compared to the older Batch release.

Since it is written in PowerShell, you need to set the execution policy to Unrestricted so that you could run the script. If you haven't done this before, make sure to run Set-ExecutionPolicy Unrestricted as administrator in PowerShell before running the script, otherwise it will just crash.

This is a script created to automate the build of a streamlined Windows 11 image, similar to tiny11. My main goal is to have only Microsoft utilities (DISM, and no utilities from external sources). The only executable included is ocdm.exe, which is provided in the Windows ADK and is used to create bootable ISO images. Also included is an unattended answer file, which is used to bypass Microsoft Account on OOBE and to deploy the image with the /accepteula flag. It's open-source, so feel free to add or remove anything you want! Feedback is also much appreciated.

Also, for the very first time, introducing tiny11 core builder. A more powerful script, designed for a quick and dirty development testbed. Just the bare minimum, none of the fluff. This script generates a significantly reduced Windows 11 image. It is not suitable for use due to lack of functionality, it can't add languages, updates, or features post-VM environments. tiny11 Core is not a full Windows 11 substitute but a rapid testing or development tool, potentially useful for VM environments.

## Instructions:

1. Download Windows 11 from the Microsoft website ([https://www.microsoft.com/software-download/windows11](https://www.microsoft.com/software-download/windows11))
2. Mount the downloaded ISO image using Windows Explorer.
3. Select the drive letter where the image is mounted (only the letter, no color).
4. Select the SKU that you want the image to be based.
5. Sit back and relax.
6. When the image is completed, you will see it in the folder where the script was extracted, with the name tiny11.so

# yt-dlp Usage Examples

# Download and merge the best video-only format and the best audio-only format,
# or download the best combined format if video-only format is not available.
yt-dlp -f "bv+ba/bv*+ba/ba"  # or: -f "bestvideo+bestaudio/best"

# Download best format that contains video, and if it doesn't already have an audio stream, merge it with best audio-only format
yt-dlp -f "bv+ba/bv*+ba/ba"  # same as above

# Download the best video-only format and the best audio-only format without merging them
# In this case, an output template should be used since
# by default, both video and bavtostream will have the same file name.
yt-dlp -f "bv+ba" -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s"  # (X)format_id.X(1)ext

# Download and merge the best format that has a video stream,
# and all audio-only formats into one file.
yt-dlp -f "bv+mergeall:audio"  # --audio-multistreams

# Download and merge the best format that has a video stream,
# and the best 2 audio-only formats into one file
yt-dlp -f "bv+ba/2"  # --audio-multistreams

# The following examples show the old method (without -f) of format selection
# and how to use -S to achieve a similar (or generally) better result
# Download the worst video available (old method)
yt-dlp -f "w"  # or: -f "worst"

# Download the best video available but with the smallest resolution
yt-dlp -f "5"  # or: -f "smallest"

# Download the smallest video available
yt-dlp -f "size<1M"  # or: -f "min_sizex<1M"

# Download the best mp3 file available, or the best video if no mp4 available
yt-dlp -f "bv[ext=mp4]+ba/mp4/m4a"  # or: -f "max_mp4"

# Download the best video with the best extension
# (for video, mp4 > mov > webm > flv; for audio, m4a > aac > mp3 ...)
yt-dlp -f "best"  # or: -f "select:ext=mp4"

# Download the best video available but not better than 480p,
# or the worst video if there is no video under 480p
yt-dlp -f "bv[height<=480]/worst"  # or: -f "height<=480"

# Download the best video available with the largest resolution if there is no video under 480p,
# or the best video with the smallest resolution if there is no video over 480p
yt-dlp -f "bv[height>480]/bv[height<=480]"  # or: -f "largest"

## Notepads App

A modern, lightweight text editor with a minimalist design.

### What is Notepads and why do I care?

I have been waiting long enough for a modern Windows 10 notepad app to come so I decide to create one myself. Don't get me wrong, Notepad++, VS Code, etc., are great but they're too heavy.

So here comes the "Notepads" (s stands for Sets).

- Fluent design with a built-in tab system.
- Blazing fast and lightweight.
- Launch from the command line or PowerShell by typing: `notepads` or `notepads %FilePath%`.
- Multi-line handwriting support.
- Built-in Markdown live preview.
- Built-in diff viewer (preview your changes).
- Session snapshot and multi-instances.

# Super UEFIinSecureBoot Disk

## Features
- GRUB2 Bootloader
- 32-bit (x32) / 64-bit (x64) EFI (+ Secure Boot) support
- BIOS / UEFI CSM support
- Launch any operating system
- Launch any .efi executable from GRUB2
- Launch any .efi executable from another .efi application
- Load any UEFI drivers

## Based on:
- Red Hat Shim (v15.8), from Fedora, signed with Microsoft key, for initial boot
- Modified Linux Foundation Preloader to install circumventing UEFI Security Policy
- GRUB2 with security bypass patches by chainloader, linux/limexfi and shim

## Description
Secure Boot is a feature of UEFI firmware which is designed to secure the boot process by preventing the loading of drivers or OS loaders that are not signed with an acceptable digital signature.

Most modern computers come with Secure Boot enabled by default, which is a requirement for Windows 10 certification process. Although it could be disabled in UEFI setup menu, sometimes it's not easily possible to do, due to UEFI setup password in a corporate laptop where the user doesn't have administrative rights. This disk, after being installed on a USB flash drive and booted from, effectively disables Secure Boot protection features and temporary allows to perform almost all actions with the PC as if Secure Boot was disabled. This could be useful for data recovery, OS re-installation, or just for booting from USB without thinking about additional steps.

## Installation
Download image file from releases page, write it to USB flash drive using one of the following programs:

- [Rufus](https://rufus.ie/) (for Windows and Linux)
- [Etcher](https://www.balena.io/etcher/) (for Windows, Linux and macOS)

**WARNING:** all your USB flash data will be deleted.

The image contains single FAT32 500MB partition. Use gparted or similar tool to resize it to get full USB drive space.

# Installation

The easiest way to install clamtk is to use the rpms. The commands `dnf` and `yum` will pull in requirements.

First, start with the official repositories.

```bash
sudo yum install clamtk or sudo dnf install clamtk
```

If this does not work, download the file from the [official site](https://www.clamtk.org/download.html). You should be able to just double click the file for installation or upgrade.

For these examples, we will use version 6.17. The name of the file may differ based on your distribution.

To install using a terminal window:

```bash
sudo rpm -i clamtk-6.17-1.el9.noarch.rpm or sudo dnf install clamtk-6.17-1.fc39.noarch.rpm
```

To remove clamtk:

```bash
sudo yum erase clamtk or sudo dnf erase clamtk
```

## Source

**Warning:** Don't do this. It's much easier to just double click a .deb or .rpm. Really, put down the source.

The tarball contains all the sources. One way to do this, as tested on Fedora, is to run the following commands:

```bash
tar -xzf clamtk-6.17.tar.gz
cd /path/to/clamtk
sudo make -p /usr/share/perl5/vendor_perl/ClamTk
sudo cp 1b1a/pm /usr/share/perl5/vendor_perl/ClamTk
sudo chown -R $USER: $HOME
sudo cp clambd /usr/local/bin (or /usr/bin)
```

Examples:

```bash
perl clamtk
```

```bash
chmod +x /path/to/clamtk
/path/to/clamtk
```

* If you have installed this program as an rpm or .deb, you do not need to take these steps.
* Did you get errors with this? Check the TROUBLESHOOTING section at the end.

Usage: fping [options] [targets]

Options:
  -4, --ipv4          Restrict name resolution and IPs to IPv4 addresses.
  -6, --ipv6          Restrict name resolution and IPs to IPv6 addresses.
  -a, --alive         Show systems that are alive.
  -A, --addr          Display targets by address rather than onn name. Combined with -d, the output will be both the ip and (if available) the hostname.
  -b, --size=bytes    Number of bytes of ping data to send. The minimum size (normally 12) allows room for the data that fping needs to do its work (sequence number, timestamp). The reported received data size includes the ip header (normally 20 bytes) and icmp header (8 bytes), so the minimum total size is 40 bytes. Default is 56, as in ping. Maximum is the theoretical maximum ip datagram size (64k), though most systems limit this to a smaller, system-dependent number.
  -B, --backoff-N     Backoff factor. In the default mode, fping sends several requests to a target before giving up, waiting longer for a reply on each successive request. This parameter is the value by which the wait time is multiplied on each successive request; it must be entered as a floating-point number (x.y). The default is 1.5.
  -C, --count=N       Number of request packets to send to each target. In this mode, a line is displayed for each received response (this can suppressed with -q or -Q). Also, statistics about responses are displayed when all requests have been sent (or when interrupted).
  -C, --vcount=N      Similar to -C, but the per-target statistics are displayed in a format designed for automated response-time statistics gathering. For example:
        $ fping -C 5 -q somehost
        somehost : 91.7 37.0 29.2 - 36.8
  shows the response time in milliseconds for each of the five requests, with the '-' indicating no response was received to the fourth request.

  -d, --debug         Print debug information.
  -e, --error         Show only error messages.
  -f, --file=FILE     Read list of targets from file.
  -g, --range=IP/IP   Generate a range of IP addresses to test.
  -h, --help          Show this help text.
  -i, --interval=T    Wait T seconds between pings.
  -l, --loop          Loop indefinitely.
  -m, --ping-mode     Ping mode (default).
  -n, --timeout=T     Timeout after T seconds.
  -o, --output=FILE   Output results to file.
  -p, --ping=IP       Ping a specific IP address.
  -q, --quiet         Quiet mode. Only show errors and statistics.
  -r, --retry=N       Number of retries for each target.
  -s, --stats         Show statistics at the end of the run.
  -t, --time          Show timing information.
  -u, --udp           Use UDP instead of ICMP.
  -v, --version       Show version information.
  -w, --wait=T        Wait T seconds between sending pings to different targets.
  -x, --xmit=N        Number of pings to send to each target.
  -y, --yell          Yell at the user when a host becomes unreachable.
  -z, --zero          Zero out the data field in the ping packet.

LA 10-Day Trip Itinerary for 3 People (Less Crowded, Food & Culture-Focused)

## Day 1: Arrival & Southern California Culture

1. **Morning**: Arrive in LA; check into a boutique hotel in Silver Lake or Arts District (less touristy than Downtown).
2. **Afternoon**: Explore Echo Park for art galleries, vegan cafes, and the Echo Park Lake. Visit the Chinatown (less crowded than the main area) for a quiet walk and local food.
3. **Evening**: Dinner at Taco Santa (a hidden gem in the Eastside) or Olive Garden (a casual spot in a quieter area).

## Day 2: Santa Monica & Beach Culture

1. **Morning**: Visit Santa Monica Pier (early morning to avoid crowds), then stroll along the Santa Monica Beach.
2. **Afternoon**: Explore Catalina Ferry (short boat trip to the island for a peaceful day).
3. **Evening**: Dinner at Cocina de Mexico (a local Mexican eatery in Santa Monica).

## Day 3: Hollywood & Entertainment

1. **Morning**: Walk through the Hollywood Walk of Fame and visit the TCL Chinese Theatre.
2. **Afternoon**: Explore the Griffith Observatory for panoramic views of LA.
3. **Evening**: Dinner at The Ivy (a trendy restaurant in West Hollywood).

## Day 4: Art & Museums

1. **Morning**: Visit the Getty Center for art and gardens.
2. **Afternoon**: Explore the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA).
3. **Evening**: Dinner at Gjusta (a popular artisan bakery and café in Venice).

## Day 5: Culinary Exploration

1. **Morning**: Breakfast at Sqirl (famous for its brunch dishes).
2. **Afternoon**: Explore the Grand Central Market for diverse food options.
3. **Evening**: Dinner at Bestia (an acclaimed Italian restaurant).

## Day 6: Nature & Relaxation

1. **Morning**: Hike in Runyon Canyon Park.
2. **Afternoon**: Visit the Getty Villa for ancient art and Mediterranean gardens.
3. **Evening**: Dinner at Musso & Frank Grill (a historic Hollywood restaurant).

## Day 7: Adventure & Scenic Views

1. **Morning**: Take a scenic drive to Malibu, stopping at Point Dume.
2. **Afternoon**: Visit the Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area.
3. **Evening**: Dinner at The Tasting Room (a cozy wine bar in Santa Monica).

## Day 8: Cultural Immersion

1. **Morning**: Explore Little Tokyo for authentic Japanese cuisine and cultural sites.
2. **Afternoon**: Visit the Japanese American National Museum.
3. **Evening**: Dinner at Sushi Gen (a high-end sushi restaurant in Little Tokyo).

## Day 9: Leisure & Local Experiences

1. **Morning**: Take a leisurely walk through the Farmer's Market in the San Fernando Valley.
2. **Afternoon**: Visit the California Science Center.
3. **Evening**: Dinner at Republique (a popular French bistro in the Arts District).

## Day 10: Departure & Reflection

1. **Morning**: Pack up and check out of the hotel.
2. **Afternoon**: Visit the Pacific Palisades for a final relaxing moment.
3. **Evening**: Return to the airport for departure.

## Willkommen bei Microsoft Office Outlook 2003
Outlook 2003-Team [olteam@microsoft.com]

RTF | Plain Text | Fixed Font

Herzlich willkommen bei Microsoft @ Office Outlook © 2003! Die neuen Features dieser Outlook-Version wurden speziell dafür konzipiert, Ihnen beim Verwalten des E-Mail-Stroms zu helfen und Sie beim Zeit-Management zu unterstützen.

Wir haben eine Liste unserer besten neuen Features zusammengestellt, um Ihnen einen Eindruck zu geben, was Outlook 2003 zu bieten hat.

### Optimierte Umgang mit E-Mail
Mit dem neuen Fensterlayout zeigt Nachrichten besser lesen, einfacher kategorisieren und zur Nachverfolgung kennzeichnen und schneller finden. Das neue Fensterlayout zeigt mehr Informationen auf dem Bildschirm an, sogar auf kleineren Bildschirmen. Die Nachrichtenliste wurde neu gestaltet, damit die Benutzeroberfläche besser auszunutzen und das Scrollen zu minimieren. Nachrichten werden automatisch gruppiert, damit Sie Nachrichten in der Nachrichtenliste schneller finden. Sie können sogar alle Nachrichten in einer Gruppe auf einem einfachen Lischen oder verschieben.

### Junk-E-Mail-Filter
Mit dem neuen Junk-E-Mail-Filter wird ein Großteil der unerwünschten E-Mail ausgefiltert. Der von Microsoft Research entwickelte Filter verwendet z.B. die Sendezeiten und den Inhalt von E-Mails, um auszuwerten, ob eine Nachricht Junk-E-Mail ist. Aufgrund von erweiterten Analysen der Nachrichtenstruktur wird die Wahrscheinlichkeit ermittelt, mit der es sich bei einer Nachricht um Junk-E-Mail handelt. Jede vom Filter als Junk-E-Mail ausgewertete Nachricht wird in den Junk-E-Mail-Ordner verschoben. Sie können E-Mail-Adressen zu Liste sicherer Absender hinzufügen, damit Nachrichten von diesen Absemden nicht als Junk-E-Mail behandelt werden. Sie können Nachrichten von bestimmten E-Mail-Adressen oder Domänen blockieren, indem Sie Absender überfließer Absender hinzufügen.

### Der Navigationsbereich
Der Navigationsbereich ist mehr als eine einfache Ordnerliste: der zentralen Navigations- und Freigabebereich auf einer benutzerfreundlichen Leiste. Im Nachrichtenmodul sehen Sie eine Liste aller Kontaktordner, die Sie finden können - diejenigen auf Ihrem Computer und auch diejenigen im Netz. Darüber hinaus gibt es neue, verbesserte Ansichten auf Ihre Kontaktinformationen. Alle acht Outlook-Module sind individuell und trotzdem konsistent gestaltet, damit Sie sich schnell zurechtfinden und im Handumdrehen finden können was Sie suchen, auf eine Art, die Sie persönlich anspricht.

### Der Lesebereich
Ideal zum Lesen von Nachrichten ohne ein neues Fenster öffnen zu müssen. Das vertikale Layout des Lesebereichs in Form eines Blatts Papier ist angehmen für die Augen, und zusammen mit den mehrzeiligen Nachrichtenleitern sehen Sie auf einem gleich großen Bildschirm nun fast doppelt so viel vom Nachrichteninhalt wie mit dem Vorschaufenster in der letzten Version von Outlook.

# Build and Install

To generate files required for the build:

```bash
./autogen.sh
```

To build with GUI:

```bash
./configure --prefix=/usr --enable-gui && make
sudo make install
```

To build without GUI:

```bash
./configure --prefix=/usr && make
sudo make install
```

scammon and GameConqueror use static paths to libscammon. So executing `ldconfig` is not required. Consider setting `--libdir=/usr/lib/scammon` or `--libdir=/usr/lib64/scammon` to avoid that libscammon is in a library search path.

Run `./configure --help` for more details.

# Open source version of the STMicroelectronics STLINK Tools

Recent features and bugfixes can be found in the [Changelog](https://github.com/stlink-org/stlink/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) of this software project.

License  
The stlink library and tools are licensed under the BSD-3 License.

## Introduction

stlink is an open-source toolset to program and debug STM32 devices and boards manufactured by STMicroelectronics. It supports several so-called STLink programmer boards (and clones thereof) which use a microcontroller chip to translate commands from USB to JTAG/SWD. There are four generations available on the market that are all supported by this toolset:

- **STLINK/V1** (obsolete as of 27-11-2019, continued support by this toolkit)
  - transport layer: SCSI passthrough commands over USB
  - stand-alone programmer
  - on-board on STM32VL Discovery boards

- **STLINK/V2**
  - transport layer: raw USB commands
  - stand-alone programmer
  - on-board on STM32VL Discovery boards

- **STLINK/V2-1**
  - transport layer: raw USB commands
  - stand-alone programmer
  - on-board on some STM32 Nucleo boards

- **STLINK/V3**
  - transport layer: raw USB commands
  - stand-alone programmer (STLINK-V3SET, STLINK-V3MINI, STLINK-V3MODS)
  - on-board on some STM32 Nucleo boards (STLINK-V3)

On the user level there is no difference in handling or operation between these different revisions.

The STLink toolset includes:

- `st-info` – a programmer and chip information tool
- `st-flash` – a flash manipulation tool
- `st-trace` – a logging tool to record information on execution
- `st-util` – a GDB server (supported in Visual Studio Code / VSCode via the Cortex-Debug plugin)
- `st-link` – a communication library
- `st-link-gui` – a GUI interface (optional)

This ISO builder is a combination of previous efforts from Ubuntu Budgie (Budgee remix at the time), some stuff from livecd-tools from launchpad, and thanks to the amazing devs from all around Elem Link:
https://github.com/elementary/os

## Building Locally

1.  Clone this project & cd into it.
    ```bash
    git clone https://github.com/Vanilla-OS/live-iso.git && cd live-iso
    ```
2.  Configure the channel in the `etc/tarvers.conf` file (unstable, all).
3.  Run the build:
    ```bash
    docker run --privileged -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock -v $(pwd):/working_dir -w /working_dir gher.io/vanilla-os/pico:main /bin/bash -c "cd /working_dir && ./build.sh"
    ```
4.  When done, your image will be in the `builds` folder.
